sections.content: Long Beach, California sits in one of the most competitive real estate markets in the country, yet savvy investors continue to find profitable deals here year after year. With a population of nearly 470,000 people, a major international port, a growing tech scene, and proximity to Los Angeles, Long Beach offers a rare combination of steady rental demand, property appreciation, and deal variety. Whether you are chasing wholesale assignments, fix-and-flip projects, or long-term buy-and-hold rentals, this city rewards investors who do their homework. If you are just getting started, check out our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide before diving into the local details below.
Long Beach CA Real Estate Market Overview

As of 2024, the median home price in Long Beach sits around $750,000, though that number varies significantly by neighborhood. Entry-level single-family homes in areas like North Long Beach can still be found in the $550,000 to $650,000 range, while properties in Belmont Shore or Naples Island regularly push past $1.2 million. The city's rental market is equally strong, with average monthly rents for a two-bedroom apartment hovering around $2,200 to $2,600. Vacancy rates remain below 4%, a sign that tenant demand consistently outpaces supply. For investors, this tight rental market translates directly into reliable cash flow potential, particularly on multi-family properties. You can explore current market data and active deal opportunities on our [Long Beach CA market page](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/long-beach-ca).
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Long Beach

Not every zip code in Long Beach carries the same investment potential. Understanding the micro-markets within the city is the fastest way to sharpen your deal-finding strategy. Here is a breakdown of the neighborhoods that consistently attract investor activity.
North Long Beach (90805, 90806)

North Long Beach is the most active zone for wholesalers and flippers in the city. Home prices are lower here relative to the rest of Long Beach, which creates more room between purchase price and after-repair value (ARV). Many properties in this corridor are older bungalows and craftsman homes from the 1940s and 1950s that need cosmetic or moderate rehab work. Investors who can execute a clean renovation often see ARVs in the $620,000 to $700,000 range on homes purchased at $480,000 to $520,000 — leaving meaningful profit after carrying costs and commissions.
Central Long Beach and Wrigley

The Wrigley neighborhood and central corridors offer a mix of single-family homes and small multi-family properties — duplexes and triplexes — that are ideal for buy-and-hold investors. Multi-family properties here generate gross rent multipliers (GRM) between 14 and 18, which is competitive for Southern California. For landlords looking to house-hack or build a small portfolio, this area is one of the most accessible entry points in the city.
Bixby Knolls

Bixby Knolls is Long Beach's up-and-coming neighborhood for premium flips. The area has attracted younger buyers and families priced out of the Westside of LA, pushing ARVs higher each year. Well-executed renovations on mid-century homes here can hit $850,000 to $950,000, making it a strong flip candidate for investors with larger rehab budgets. The key is finding the deal — on-market inventory moves fast, which means building an off-market pipeline is essential.

Pro Tip: In competitive neighborhoods like Bixby Knolls, the best deals rarely hit the MLS. Focus on direct mail campaigns to absentee owners, driving for dollars, and probate leads. Learning [how to find off-market real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) is one of the highest-ROI skills you can develop as a Long Beach investor.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Long Beach
Wholesale Deals

Long Beach is an active wholesale market, particularly in North Long Beach and Central Long Beach. Wholesalers typically target distressed properties — inherited homes, properties with deferred maintenance, and pre-foreclosure situations — and assign purchase contracts to cash buyers or fix-and-flip investors. Assignment fees in the Long Beach market typically range from $15,000 to $40,000 on a standard single-family deal, depending on the spread between contract price and ARV. If wholesaling is your primary strategy, our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide walks through the process step by step.
Fix-and-Flip

Flipping homes in Long Beach can generate strong returns when deals are underwritten correctly. The 70% rule is a common starting point — meaning you should pay no more than 70% of the ARV minus estimated rehab costs. For example, on a home with a $700,000 ARV and $80,000 in repairs, your maximum purchase price would be $410,000. Always run your numbers before making an offer. Use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to quickly estimate after-repair value based on comparable sales in the area.
Buy-and-Hold Rentals

Long Beach's rental market is one of the strongest in Southern California. Strong employment anchors — including the Port of Long Beach, California State University Long Beach, and a growing healthcare sector — keep tenant demand high. Multi-family properties remain the preferred vehicle for long-term investors, and duplexes in the $800,000 to $1,000,000 range can produce monthly rents of $4,500 to $6,000 combined, depending on unit size and condition. Cash-on-cash returns in the 4% to 6% range are realistic with proper financing and value-add improvements.
In markets like Long Beach, the deal is made at the purchase price, not the sale price. Buy right and almost every exit strategy works. Buy wrong and no amount of renovation will save your margins.
Long Beach Real Estate Market Trends to Watch in 2024

items: Interest rate sensitivity: Higher mortgage rates have slowed buyer activity, creating more negotiating room for cash investors and those using hard money loans.
Rising insurance costs: California property insurance has increased sharply in recent years. Factor in 20-30% higher insurance premiums when underwriting deals compared to two years ago.
Port-driven demand: The Port of Long Beach handled record cargo volumes in 2023, supporting employment and household formation in the area.
Rent control awareness: Long Beach has local rent control ordinances that apply to certain older multi-family properties. Always verify rent control applicability before acquiring rental properties.
Population stability: Despite broader California outmigration trends, Long Beach has maintained a stable population base due to its job diversity and relative affordability compared to LA proper.

sections.content: Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Long Beach

Long Beach attracts interest from investors across the country, particularly from states like Texas, Arizona, and Nevada where capital gains from home sales have been reinvested into California. If you are investing remotely, the following strategies will help you compete with local operators.

items: Build a local team first: You need a reliable real estate agent who works with investors, a local contractor with references, and a property manager before you close your first deal.
Use data to find deals before visiting: Platforms like AIWholesail let you identify distressed properties, absentee owners, and pre-foreclosure situations in Long Beach before you ever board a plane.
Understand California-specific laws: Disclosure requirements, tenant protections, and transfer taxes in California are more complex than many other states. Consult a local real estate attorney.

Focus on neighborhoods with clear comps: As an out-of-state investor, stick to neighborhoods where sold comparables are plentiful and consistent. Avoid unique properties or hyper-local micro-markets until you know the city well.

Analyze every deal thoroughly: Never skip due diligence because a deal looks good on paper. Learn [how to analyze real estate deals like a pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) to make sure your numbers hold up under scrutiny.

Run your wholesale numbers precisely: Use our free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to stress-test purchase prices, rehab estimates, and projected profits before submitting any offer.

sections.content: Pro Tip: When evaluating Long Beach deals remotely, order a virtual walkthrough or hire a local inspector for a pre-offer assessment. Spending $200 to $300 on an early inspection can save you from a $50,000 mistake on a property with hidden foundation or plumbing issues.
Is Long Beach Still Worth Investing In?

The short answer is yes — but with discipline. Long Beach is not a market where deals fall into your lap. Competition is real, margins require careful management, and local regulations add a layer of complexity that some markets do not have. But the fundamentals remain strong: population density, employment diversity, port infrastructure, and proximity to one of the largest metro areas in the country all support long-term property values. Investors who focus on off-market sourcing, conservative underwriting, and strong local teams consistently find profitable deals in Long Beach year after year.
